literal: That year, Prince Chuo of Nanyang was killed.
idiomatic: That year Prince Chuo of Nanyang was put to death.

literal: In the third month of spring of the sixth year, on the yihai day, the imperial carriage arrived from Jinyang.
idiomatic: In the third month of spring of the sixth year, on the yihai day, the emperor returned from Jinyang.

literal: On the dingchou day, the sorcerer-rebel Zheng Zirao was boiled alive in the marketplace.
idiomatic: On the dingchou day, the sorcerer-rebel Zheng Zirao was boiled alive in the public marketplace.

literal: That month, envoys from Zhou came on a diplomatic visit.
idiomatic: That month envoys from Zhou arrived on a diplomatic visit.

literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the gengzi day, Director of the Secretariat Yang Xiuzhi was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the gengzi day, Director of the Secretariat Yang Xiuzhi was appointed right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: On the guimao day, the Mojie sent envoys to pay court tribute.
idiomatic: On the guimao day, envoys from Mojie arrived to pay court tribute.

literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the jiaxu day, the emperor proceeded to Jinyang.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the jiaxu day, the emperor went to Jinyang.

literal: In the eighth month, on the dingyou day, the six provinces of Ji, Ding, Zhao, You, Cang, and Ying suffered great floods.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the dingyou day, Ji, Ding, Zhao, You, Cang, and Ying Provinces were struck by severe flooding.

literal: That month, Zhou forces entered Luochuan, encamped at Mangshan, pressed the attack on Luoyang, sent fire ships to burn the pontoon bridge, and the river bridge was cut off.
idiomatic: That month Zhou troops entered Luochuan, encamped at Mangshan, and pressed the siege of Luoyang; fire ships burned the pontoon bridge and severed the river crossing.

literal: In the intercalary month, on the jichou day, Right Chancellor Gao Anaggon was dispatched from Jinyang to meet them; his army halted at Heyang, and the Zhou forces fled by night.
idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the jichou day, Right Chancellor Gao Anaggon was sent from Jinyang to oppose them; his army halted at Heyang, and the Zhou troops withdrew under cover of night.

literal: On the gengchen day, Minister of Works Zhao Yanshen was made Minister over the Masses, and Hulu Alieluo was made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: On the gengchen day, Minister of Works Zhao Yanshen was appointed minister over the masses, and Hulu Alieluo was made minister of works.

literal: On the xinsi day, because military and state expenses were insufficient, taxes were levied on market tolls, boats and carts, mountains and marshes, salt and iron, and shops, with varying rates of severity, and the prohibition on wine was lifted.
idiomatic: On the xinsi day, with military and state coffers empty, the court taxed market tolls, transport, natural resources, salt and iron, and shops at graded rates, and lifted the ban on wine.

literal: In the first month of spring of the seventh year, on the renchen day, an edict declared that since the previous autumn, wherever people rendered destitute by flood and famine could not support themselves, local authorities were to entrust them to major monasteries and wealthy households to preserve their lives.
idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the seventh year, on the renchen day, an edict ordered that flood and famine victims unable to support themselves since the previous autumn be placed with major monasteries and wealthy households for relief.

literal: On the jiayin day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
idiomatic: On the jiayin day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

literal: On the yimao day, the imperial carriage arrived from Jinyang.
idiomatic: On the yimao day, the emperor returned from Jinyang.

literal: In the second month, on the xinyou day, unmarried women of miscellaneous households aged fourteen to twenty were all rounded up and sent to the capital; any family head who concealed them was sentenced to death.
idiomatic: In the second month, on the xinyou day, unmarried women of miscellaneous households between fourteen and twenty were conscripted and sent to the capital, and any family head who hid them faced execution.

literal: In the second month, on the bingyin day, a wind rose from the northwest, tearing off roofs and uprooting trees; after five days it ceased.
idiomatic: In the second month, on the bingyin day, a windstorm from the northwest tore off roofs and uprooted trees and did not subside until the fifth day.

literal: In the sixth month of summer, on the wushen day, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month of summer, the wushen day, there was a solar eclipse.

literal: On the gengshen day, Minister over the Masses Zhao Yanshen died.
idiomatic: On the gengshen day, Minister over the Masses Zhao Yanshen died.

literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the dingchou day, heavy rains fell for many days.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the dingchou day, torrential rains fell for many days.

literal: That month, because of flood damage, envoys were dispatched to tour and succor displaced households.
idiomatic: That month, because of flooding, envoys were sent to tour the provinces and aid displaced households.

literal: In the eighth month, on the dingmao day, the emperor proceeded to Jinyang.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the dingmao day, the emperor went to Jinyang.

literal: A pheasant alighted on the imperial seat; it was caught, and the officials dared not report it.
idiomatic: A pheasant alighted on the imperial throne; it was caught, but the officials dared not report the omen.

literal: An edict ordered the Handan Palace to be built.
idiomatic: An edict ordered construction of the Handan Palace.

literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the bingchen day, the emperor conducted a great hunt at Qilian Pool.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the bingchen day, the emperor held a great hunt at Qilian Pool.

literal: Zhou forces attacked Jin Province.
idiomatic: Zhou forces attacked Jin Province.

literal: On the guihai day, the emperor returned to Jinyang.
idiomatic: On the guihai day, the emperor returned to Jinyang.

literal: On the jiazi day, troops were mobilized and massed at the Jin Shrine.
idiomatic: On the jiazi day, the army was mobilized and assembled at the Jin Shrine.

literal: On the gengwu day, the emperor set out from Jinyang.
idiomatic: On the gengwu day, the emperor marched out from Jinyang.

literal: On the guiyou day, the emperor drew up his battle lines and advanced to Jiqiyuan, facing Prince Xian of Zhou across the field; they stood opposite each other until night without fighting, and the Zhou army withdrew its formations and retreated.
idiomatic: On the guiyou day, the emperor formed battle lines and advanced to Jiqiyuan, facing Prince Xian of Zhou; the two armies faced off until nightfall without engaging, and the Zhou troops then withdrew.

literal: In the eleventh month, Emperor Wu of Zhou withdrew to Chang'an, leaving a detached force to hold Jin Province.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month Emperor Wu of Zhou withdrew to Chang'an, leaving a detached force to garrison Jin Province.

literal: Gao Anaggon and others besieged the city of Jin Province.
idiomatic: Gao Anaggon and others laid siege to Jin Province.

literal: On the wuyin day, the emperor reached the siege camp.
idiomatic: On the wuyin day, the emperor arrived at the siege lines.

literal: In the twelfth month, on the wushen day, Emperor Wu of Zhou came to relieve Jin Province; on the gengxu day they fought south of the city, and our army was routed.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the wushen day, Emperor Wu of Zhou marched to relieve Jin Province; on the gengxu day battle was joined south of the city, and the Northern Qi army was routed.

literal: The emperor abandoned the army and fled first.
idiomatic: The emperor abandoned his army and fled ahead of the troops.

literal: On the guichou day, he entered Jinyang, anxious and fearful, not knowing where to turn.
idiomatic: On the guichou day he entered Jinyang, stricken with fear and at a loss for what to do.

literal: On the jiayin day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
idiomatic: On the jiayin day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

literal: The emperor said to the court ministers: "The Zhou army is very strong—what shall we do?"
idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers: "The Zhou army is overwhelming—what are we to do?"

literal: All the ministers said that Heaven's mandate had not changed and that gaining here and losing there had been the way since antiquity.
idiomatic: The ministers replied as one that Heaven's mandate had not shifted and that kingdoms had always known both victory and defeat.

literal: They said one should halt all levies, reassure court and country, gather the scattered troops, and fight to the death with one's back to the city walls to preserve the altars of state.
idiomatic: They urged him to suspend every tax, steady court and countryside, rally the broken army, and make a last stand behind the city walls to save the realm.

literal: The emperor still hesitated and wished to flee north to Shuozhou.
idiomatic: The emperor remained undecided and wanted to flee north to Shuozhou.

literal: Thereupon he left Prince Yanzong of Ande, Prince Xiaogong of Guangning, and others to defend Jinyang.
idiomatic: He then left Prince Yanzong of Ande, Prince Xiaogong of Guangning, and others to hold Jinyang.

literal: If Jinyang could not be held, he then intended to flee to the Turks.
idiomatic: If Jinyang fell, he planned to flee to the Turks.

literal: All the ministers said this could not be done, but the emperor would not heed their words.
idiomatic: Every minister protested, but the emperor refused to listen.

literal: Opening Ceremony Equaling the Three Dukes Heba Fu'en, Feng Fuxiang, Murong Zhongkui, and more than thirty other palace guards and close attendants fled west to the Zhou army.
idiomatic: Heba Fu'en, Feng Fuxiang, Murong Zhongkui, and more than thirty other palace guards and intimate attendants deserted westward to the Zhou camp.

literal: On the yimao day, an edict ordered recruitment of troops and dispatched Prince Yanzong of Ande to the left and Prince Xiaogong of Guangning to the right.
idiomatic: On the yimao day, an edict called for levies and placed Prince Yanzong of Ande on the left flank and Prince Xiaogong of Guangning on the right.

literal: Yanzong entered to see the emperor, who told him he wished to flee north to Shuozhou.
idiomatic: Yanzong came before the emperor, who confided that he meant to flee north to Shuozhou.

literal: Yanzong wept and remonstrated, but the emperor would not listen.
idiomatic: Yanzong pleaded through tears, but the emperor would not be moved.

literal: The emperor secretly dispatched Wang Kangde and the eunuch Qi Shao and others to escort the empress dowager and crown prince north to Shuozhou.
idiomatic: The emperor secretly sent Wang Kangde and the eunuch Qi Shao to convey the empress dowager and crown prince north to Shuozhou.

literal: On the bingchen day, the emperor visited the army south of the city to encourage the troops; that night he wished to slip away, but the generals would not follow.
idiomatic: On the bingchen day the emperor went to the southern camp to rally the troops; that night he tried to flee, but his generals refused.

literal: On the dingsi day, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and the seventh year of Wuping was changed to the first year of Longhua.
idiomatic: On the dingsi day a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed from Wuping 7 to Longhua 1.

literal: That same day, Mu Tipo surrendered to Zhou.
idiomatic: That same day Mu Tipo defected to Zhou.

literal: An edict removed Prince Yanzong of Ande from office and made him grand chancellor, entrusting him with defense; Yanzong accepted through tears.
idiomatic: An edict relieved Prince Yanzong of Ande of his post and made him grand chancellor with full authority over the defense; Yanzong accepted the charge in tears.

literal: The emperor then cut through the Wulong Gate by night and went out, intending to flee to the Turks; many of his attendants scattered.
idiomatic: That night the emperor cut through the Wulong Gate intending to flee to the Turks, and most of his attendants scattered.

literal: Leading Army Commander Mei Sheng seized the bridle and remonstrated, whereupon he turned back toward Ye.
idiomatic: Leading Army Commander Mei Sheng seized his horse's bridle and pleaded with him, and the emperor turned back toward Ye.

literal: At that time only Gao Anaggon and a dozen or so horsemen remained; Prince Xiaogong of Guangning and Prince Yandao of Xiangcheng caught up afterward, and they had several dozen men traveling together.
idiomatic: Only Gao Anaggon and a dozen riders were still with him; Prince Xiaogong of Guangning and Prince Yandao of Xiangcheng soon joined them, bringing their party to several dozen men.

literal: On the wuwu day, Yanzong, yielding to the will of the assembly, immediately took the throne at Jinyang and changed Longhua to the first year of Dechang.
idiomatic: On the wuwu day Yanzong, bowing to the will of the assembly, immediately ascended the throne at Jinyang and changed the era name to Dechang 1.

literal: On the gengshen day, the emperor entered Ye.
idiomatic: On the gengshen day the emperor entered Ye.

literal: On the xinyou day, Yanzong fought the Zhou army at Jinyang, was routed, and was captured by the Zhou forces.
idiomatic: On the xinyou day Yanzong fought the Zhou army at Jinyang, was defeated, and was taken prisoner.

literal: The emperor ordered recruitment of men with heavy rewards of office and bounty; though he spoke thus, in the end he furnished nothing.
idiomatic: The emperor called for recruits with lavish promises of rank and reward, but in the end provided nothing.

literal: Prince Xiaogong of Guangning memorialized asking that palace women and treasures be distributed to the troops, and the emperor was displeased.
idiomatic: Prince Xiaogong of Guangning petitioned to distribute palace women and treasures among the troops, and the emperor took offense.

literal: Hulu Xiaoqing, holding delegated authority at court, wore armor to direct affairs; he asked the emperor to address the troops in person, drafted a speech for him, and said he ought to speak with generous tears to stir the hearts of the men.
idiomatic: Hulu Xiaoqing, wielding delegated authority at court, appeared in armor to direct affairs; he urged the emperor to address the troops in person, drafted a speech for him, and said he should speak through generous tears to stir their hearts.

literal: When the emperor came out before the assembly and was about to address them, he no longer remembered what he had been told to say; he burst into loud laughter instead, and those around him all guffawed with him, so that the soldiers entirely lost heart.
idiomatic: When the emperor appeared before the troops and tried to speak, he forgot every word he had been given and burst out laughing; his attendants joined in, and the soldiers' morale collapsed entirely.

literal: Thereupon from grand chancellor downward, grand tutor, the three preceptors, grand marshal, grand general, and the three dukes and other offices all had their quotas increased and appointments made, some to three or four men each, beyond counting.
idiomatic: Thereupon posts from grand chancellor down through grand tutor, the three preceptors, grand marshal, grand general, and the three dukes were multiplied, some offices filled three or four at a time, beyond number.

literal: On the jiazi day, the empress dowager arrived by the northern route.
idiomatic: On the jiazi day the empress dowager arrived by the northern road.

literal: Civil and military officials of the first rank and above were summoned into the Zhuhua Gate, given wine and food, provided paper and brush, and asked for plans to resist Zhou.
idiomatic: He summoned civil and military officials of the first rank and above to the Zhuhua Gate, feasted them, supplied paper and brush, and asked how Zhou might be resisted.

literal: The ministers each offered different proposals, and the emperor did not know whom to follow.
idiomatic: Each minister offered a different plan, and the emperor could not decide whom to follow.

literal: He then summoned Gao Yuanhai, Song Shisu, Lu Sidao, Li Delin, and others, intending to deliberate on abdicating the throne to the crown prince.
idiomatic: He then summoned Gao Yuanhai, Song Shisu, Lu Sidao, Li Delin, and others to discuss abdicating in favor of the crown prince.

literal: Earlier, diviners of celestial signs had said there would be a dynastic change; in the end they followed the precedent of the Tian Tong era and transferred the throne to Youzhu.
idiomatic: Earlier court diviners had foretold a change of dynasty; in the end the court followed the Tian Tong precedent and transferred the throne to Youzhu.

literal: Youzhu, personal name Heng, was the emperor's eldest son.
idiomatic: Youzhu, whose personal name was Heng, was the emperor's eldest son.

literal: His mother was Empress Mu; he was born at Ye in the sixth month of the first year of Wuping.
idiomatic: His mother was Empress Mu; he was born at Ye in the sixth month of the first year of the Wuping era.

literal: In the tenth month of that year he was established as crown prince.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year he was formally established as crown prince.

literal: In the first month of spring of the second year of Longhua, on the yihai day, he immediately took the throne; he was eight years old; the era name was changed to Chengguang 1; a general amnesty was proclaimed; the empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager; the emperor became retired emperor; and the empress became retired empress.
idiomatic: In the first month of spring of Longhua 2, on the yihai day, he immediately ascended the throne at the age of eight; the era was renamed Chengguang 1; a general amnesty was proclaimed; the empress dowager was elevated to grand empress dowager; the former emperor became retired emperor; and the empress became retired empress.

literal: Thereupon Yellow Gate Gentleman Yan Zhitui, Masters of Writing Gentleman Xue Daohang, Palace Attendant Chen Dexin, and others urged the retired emperor to go beyond the Yellow River to recruit troops and renew strategic planning; if that failed, they should flee south and submit to Chen—and he agreed.
idiomatic: Yellow Gate Gentleman Yan Zhitui, Masters of Writing Gentleman Xue Daohang, Palace Attendant Chen Dexin, and others then urged the retired emperor to cross the Yellow River to raise troops and regroup; if that failed, they should flee south to Chen—and he agreed.

literal: On the dingchou day, the grand empress dowager and retired empress left Ye first and hastened to Ji Province.
idiomatic: On the dingchou day the grand empress dowager and retired empress departed Ye ahead of the court and hurried toward Ji Province.

literal: As the Zhou army pressed closer, on the guimao day Youzhu again fled east from Ye.
idiomatic: As Zhou forces closed in, on the guimao day Youzhu fled east from Ye once more.

literal: On the jichou day, the Zhou army reached Zimo Bridge.
idiomatic: On the jichou day the Zhou army reached Zimo Bridge.

literal: On the guisi day, the western gate of the city was burned.
idiomatic: On the guisi day the western gate of the city was set ablaze.

literal: The retired emperor fled east with a little more than a hundred horsemen.
idiomatic: The retired emperor fled east with barely a hundred riders.

literal: On the yihai day, he crossed the river and entered Ji Province.
idiomatic: On the yihai day he crossed the river and entered Ji Province.

literal: That same day Youzhu abdicated the throne to Grand Chancellor Prince Ji of Rencheng and ordered Palace Attendant Hulu Xiaoqing to deliver the abdication document and imperial seal and cord to Ying Province; Xiaoqing instead took them to Zhou.
idiomatic: That same day Youzhu abdicated in favor of Grand Chancellor Prince Ji of Rencheng and ordered Palace Attendant Hulu Xiaoqing to convey the abdication text and imperial seal and cord to Ying Province—but Xiaoqing delivered them to Zhou instead.

literal: Prince Ji also issued an edict in his own name honoring the retired emperor as supreme retired emperor and Youzhu as guardian king of the realm.
idiomatic: Prince Ji also issued an edict in his own name, elevating the retired emperor to supreme retired emperor and naming Youzhu guardian king of the realm.

literal: The grand empress dowager was left at Ji Province, and Gao Anaggon was dispatched to hold the city.
idiomatic: The grand empress dowager was left at Ji Province with Gao Anaggon assigned to hold the city.

literal: The retired emperor, the empress, and Youzhu fled to Qing Province, accompanied by Han Changluan, Deng Yan, and several dozen others.
idiomatic: The retired emperor, the empress, and Youzhu fled toward Qing Province with Han Changluan, Deng Yan, and several dozen followers.

literal: Once the retired emperor reached Qing Province, he immediately planned entry into Chen.
idiomatic: Once the retired emperor reached Qing Province, he immediately set about planning flight into Chen.

literal: But Gao Anaggon summoned the Zhou army, agreeing to deliver the Qi ruler alive, yet repeatedly sent word saying the enemy was still far off and that he had already had the bridges and roads burned.
idiomatic: But Gao Anaggon had summoned the Zhou army, promising to deliver the Qi ruler alive, while repeatedly reporting that the enemy was still distant and that he had already burned the bridges and roads.

literal: For this reason the retired emperor halted and delayed.
idiomatic: That is why the retired emperor paused and delayed his flight.

literal: The Zhou army suddenly reached Qing Province; the retired emperor, in desperate straits and about to withdraw into Chen, placed a gold pouch behind his saddle; with Changluan, the consort, and a dozen or so riders he reached Deng Village south of Qing Province and was captured by the Zhou general Yuchi Gang.
idiomatic: The Zhou army suddenly appeared at Qing Province; cornered and about to slip into Chen, the retired emperor hung a gold pouch from his saddle and rode south with Changluan, his consort, and a dozen followers to Deng Village south of the city, where Zhou general Yuchi Gang seized them.

literal: They were sent to Ye; Emperor Wu of Zhou received the retired emperor with the courtesies due a guest of equal rank; the empress dowager, Youzhu, and the princes were all sent to Chang'an, and the retired emperor was enfeoffed as Duke of Wen.
idiomatic: They were sent to Ye, where Emperor Wu of Zhou received the retired emperor with the courtesies due an equal; the empress dowager, Youzhu, and the princes were all sent to Chang'an, and the retired emperor was enfeoffed as Duke of Wen.

literal: In the seventh year of Jiande he was falsely accused of plotting rebellion with Governor of Yizhou Mu Tipo; Yanzong and several dozen others, without distinction of age, were all granted death; of Shenwu's descendants only one or two remained.
idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Jiande era he was falsely accused of plotting rebellion with Mu Tipo, governor of Yizhou; Yanzong and dozens of others, young and old alike, were put to death; of Shenwu's descendants only one or two survived.

literal: By the end of the Daxiang era, Yang Xiuzhi, Chen Dexin, and others petitioned Grand Chancellor Duke Sui, asking permission to gather the remains for burial; permission was granted, and they were buried at Hongdu Stream on the northern plain of Chang'an.
idiomatic: By the end of the Daxiang era Yang Xiuzhi, Chen Dexin, and others petitioned Grand Chancellor the Duke of Sui for permission to bury the remains; he consented, and they were interred at Hongdu Stream on the northern plain of Chang'an.

literal: The emperor was good and well behaved from childhood; when grown he studied composition to some degree, established the Forest of Letters Hall, and gathered literary men there.
idiomatic: As a boy the emperor was well behaved; as he grew he took up literary composition, established the Forest of Letters Hall, and gathered scholars there.

literal: Yet his speech was halting, he lacked resolution, and he disliked meeting court officials.
idiomatic: Yet he spoke haltingly, lacked firm purpose, and disliked receiving court officials.

literal: Unless they were favorites or intimate companions, he never exchanged words with them; he was timid and could not bear to be looked at—whoever gazed at him he at once rebuked in anger.
idiomatic: Unless they were favorites or intimate companions he never spoke with them; craven and unable to endure being watched, he would fly into a rage at anyone who looked at him.

literal: Those who submitted memorials—even the three dukes and chief ministers—might not raise their eyes to look at him; they could only sketch the main points, then flee out in alarm.
idiomatic: Even the three dukes and chief ministers reporting to him dared not meet his gaze; they could only outline the gist of their business and flee in alarm.

literal: Whenever there were calamities, banditry, or flood and drought, he never reduced expenditures or humbled himself; he only ordered vegetarian feasts at various places, taking that as cultivation of virtue.
idiomatic: Whenever disaster, banditry, flood, or drought struck, he never cut spending or humbled himself; he merely ordered vegetarian offerings here and there, calling that moral cultivation.

literal: He trusted shamans implicitly and knew no method of prayer or expiation beyond them.
idiomatic: He put blind faith in shamans and knew no remedy for prayer or expiation beyond them.

literal: At first when the Prince of Langye raised troops, the informant wrongly said Kudivolian had rebelled, and the emperor said this must be Renwei.
idiomatic: When the Prince of Langye first rose in arms, an informant wrongly reported that Kudivolian had rebelled, and the emperor said this must be Renwei.

literal: Later, after Hulu Guang died, the military officers recommended Gao Sihao as fit for grand general, and the emperor said Sihao was fond of rebelling.
idiomatic: Later, after Hulu Guang's death, the military officers recommended Gao Sihao for grand general, and the emperor said Sihao was always ready to rebel.

literal: On every occasion it proved exactly as he had said.
idiomatic: On every occasion events proved exactly as he had predicted.
